LESSON: FRACTIONS

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade four
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: Numbers
Topic 1.6: Fractions
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 6

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Fractions, part of Numbers in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade four MATHEMATICS.

Key inquiry question: How do you usefractions in real life? 2. How can you represent fractions?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. Discuss in purposive pairs or groups the top (numerator) and bottom (denominator) numbers in a fraction and share with other groups. Those with speech difficulties could use Alternative and Augmentative modes of Communication-AAC (residual speech/ digital devices 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. Discuss in purposive pairs or groups the top (numerator) and bottom (denominator) numbers in a fraction and share with other groups. Those with speech difficulties could use Alternative and Augmentative modes of Communication-AAC (residual speech/ digital devices 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Fractions together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Self-efficacy: Learner confidently illustrates fractions as part of a whole or part of a group using cut outs,

counters or clock face.

Values:
Responsibility: Learner shares roles while illustrating proper, improper and mixed fractions as part of a

whole or as part of a group using paper cut outs or counters.

17

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Learner assists each other to change mixed fractions to improper fractions to enhance peer education.

Link to other subjects

The learner is able to relate fractions as part of a whole or part of a group using cut outs, counters or clock face

to mixtures in Science and Technology
